lesson: Build round plates and rims as one rotate_extrude() profile; a union of coincident cylinders leaves a 4-face seam edge and a non-watertight STL.
A part with features on both faces (boss below, hub above) cannot print flat: split the smaller feature into its own part (e.g. a spacer ring) instead of adding supports.
Arched clamps/straps print on their side as a 2-D profile; standing them up makes the crown a 90 deg overhang.
Pocket ceilings printed face-down are flat overhangs the area metric under-reports: give pockets 45 deg conical walls and keep any remaining bridge under ~30 mm.
Sink the lid bearing boss into a recess in the drive gear: it saves ~4 mm of base height versus stacking bearing above gear.
Orient a gearmotor tangentially (can along the base's circumference) so the base diameter is set by the plate gear, not by motor length.
Run an interference view (intersection() of every assembled pair, must be empty) before shipping: a lid locating lip crossing the screw bosses is invisible in renders but shows as ~120 mm3 overlap.
Right-angle drives for FDM: use a crown (face) gear + spur pinion, not a bevel pair; it prints teeth-up with no overhang and tolerates +-0.5 mm axial pinion position.
When a pinion meshes a crown/face gear on its centre line, phase the pinion by half a tooth pitch (180/N degrees) or tooth lands on tooth; the interference view catches it.
Slimmest vertical-axis stack: fixed post, one bearing inside each rotating part, spacer tube between inner races; height is then set by the pinion OD, not by bearing stacking.
Keep >= 2 mm between a rotating disc rim and any static wall; a 0.5 mm graze shows up as <1 mm3 in the interference view but will click when printed.
Anything displayed on a turntable goes on the rotation axis with a positive locating recess in the plate; an off-axis stand orbits and reads badly on camera.
Card stands for camera work: lean the slot 10-15 deg back, keep the front lip under ~12 mm with a finger notch, and size the slot for the sleeve (3 mm), not the bare card.
